newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage rates fall to 8-month low.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage rates fall to 8-month low.

text.p: Mortgage rates fell this week to the lowest levels in more than eight months as the economy continued to grow steadily without much inflation, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. said Thursday.

Fixed-rate mortgage rates fell for the fourth consecutive week in the week ended Nov. 15. Thirty-year mortgages avaraged 7.59 percent, the lowest since 7.38 percent in the week ended March 8, 1996. The rate was 7.67 percent last week.
Fifteen-year loans fell to 7.11 percent, the lowest since 6.87 percent in the March 8 week. Last week the rate averaged 7.20 percent.
Adjustable-rate mortgages inched down to 5.52 percent from 5.56 percent. The rate was also the lowest since the March 8 week, when it averaged 5.40 percent.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.35 percent, the 15-year 6.86 percent, and the adjustable loan 5.65 percent.

"With the economy slow but stable, there is little fear of inflation in the market and this is reflected in lower interest rates again this week," said Robert Van Order, Freddie Mac chief economist. "Indications are good that we may well see interest rates even lower next week."
The Labour Department reported that October consumer prices rose 0.3 percent, in line with expectations. On Wednesday the Federal Reserve held interest rates unchanged.

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average of 1.8 percent in fees and points on 30- and 15-year loans, both up from 1.7 percent last week. They charged 1.4 percent on adjustable loans, unchanged from last week.
Separately, the Mortgage Bankers Association of America said the volume of mortgage applications rose 2.9 percent in the week ended Nov. 8.
The volume of applications to refinance mortgages rose 12.1 percent in the latest week while applications for new mortgages fell 0.3 percent.
